rv.q: Barbot’s audacious, quick-witted play keeps constantly in the air.
Zayas deftly navigates the wild tonal shifts in Barbot’s script, sacrificing neither humor nor gravity in this grim farce.
Barbot prompts lots of meaty questions with the play and it was refreshing to see a story on stage I had not heard before.

cn.t: Critics praise this hallucinogenic history play about forgotten Puerto Rican nationalists who attempted to assassinate Truman, finding it an excellent and symbolically rich exploration of American expansion and migration.
